profile.address: 20845, Sockeye Place, Bend, Deschutes County, Oregon, 97701
profile.reading:
OR01 is US Signal's data center in Bend, Oregon, located at 20845 Sockeye Place in Deschutes County. US Signal is a Michigan-based provider of cloud, colocation, disaster recovery, and managed network services that operates a portfolio of data centers across the Midwest and, with this site, the Pacific Northwest. According to the operator's own published facility page, the Bend building was constructed in 2010 and is rated at Tier 3 resiliency, meaning its power and cooling paths are designed with concurrent maintainability so that planned maintenance on any single system component should not require shutting down the facility. The building also carries LEED certification, indicating it was designed or renovated to recognized green-building energy and environmental standards.

On the power side, US Signal publishes a 2,000 kilowatt standby generator plant configured N+1, meaning one additional unit of backup capacity beyond what is needed to carry the load, and a 2,500 kVA utility electrical feed from the local grid. Cooling is handled by a 256 ton HVAC plant, also configured with N+1 redundancy, while the facility's UPS battery backup is described as 2N, a fully mirrored redundant configuration considered a higher standard than N+1. Fire protection combines VESDA very early smoke detection with a clean agent suppression system that extinguishes fire without damaging electronic equipment, and physical access is controlled biometrically with recorded video surveillance. US Signal advertises a 99.999 percent uptime service level agreement for the facility and lists six on-net telecommunications carriers with managed, BGP-routed bandwidth over a redundant backbone.

The operator's page does not publish a specific total square footage, whitespace figure, or IT critical load in kilowatts for OR01, listing those fields as unspecified rather than providing numbers. Bend itself is a mid-sized city in Central Oregon that has drawn technology and outdoor recreation-adjacent business investment over the past two decades, and a Tier 3, LEED-certified colocation facility there gives regional businesses, along with customers seeking geographic diversity from more crowded data center markets, a redundant, carrier-connected option away from the West Coast's major metro hubs.

US Signal markets OR01 as part of a wider network of company-owned and operated facilities rather than as a single standalone site, positioning Bend alongside its other Midwest locations as an option for customers who want production workloads and backup or disaster recovery copies housed in different regions of the country at once. For a company built around colocation, cloud, and managed network services, publishing concrete, named engineering figures for Tier rating, generator capacity, and cooling redundancy, as US Signal does here, is itself a form of marketing aimed at technically sophisticated buyers who evaluate facilities on exactly those terms before committing infrastructure to a given site.

profile.research_note: Operator's own OR01 Bend page shows Tier 3 resiliency and LEED certification, opened 2010, 2,000kW N+1 generator (standby, not IT capacity), 2500kVA utility feed (excluded). IT critical load and total/whitespace sqft fields on the page itself are literal placeholder zeros -- treated as unpublished, not guessed.

reading.body:
US Signal's Bend facility is a Tier 3 colocation site opened in 2010 with redundant power and cooling systems designed to remain operational during maintenance on any single component. The operator publishes a 2 MW N+1 standby generator plant and 256 ton HVAC capacity configured with redundancy, but does not publish its IT critical load in kilowatts or total usable square footage. Without published IT load, the facility's actual AI hosting capacity cannot be estimated from the available data.

OR01 holds LEED certification, qualifying it as a facility designed to recognized energy efficiency standards. The operator markets the site as part of a regional network for customers seeking geographic diversity and disaster recovery options rather than as a hyperscale compute destination, and advertises six on-net telecommunications carriers with BGP routing. The facility serves colocation, cloud, and managed network services rather than being dedicated to AI training or inference.

In Oregon, 133 facilities are mapped but only 8 publish capacity figures totaling 156.6 MW. OR01 does not appear in that published count because US Signal has not disclosed its IT load. Bend is the ninth-ranked Oregon facility by published megawatts among those that disclose capacity, though this ranking applies only to the eight sites that do publish and thus measures the absence of disclosure rather than actual size. For readers assessing whether this campus matters to AI scaling, the unpublished load figure means its contribution to Oregon's grid-constrained AI infrastructure cannot be quantified from operator disclosures.
